info.name: Workstation Health Dashboard — Cloudflare Speed Test
info.description:
The HTTP endpoints the dashboard's network speed test measures against (app/renderer/speedtest.js), with test scripts.

Run the whole collection in the Collection Runner (or `npx newman run`), in order. Each request logs its measurement to the console.

These are single-request, single-stream measurements, and Postman's response time includes connection setup and time-to-first-byte. They are good for checking the endpoints' behaviour, not for benchmarking the link: the app itself uses parallel streams and counts only bytes moved over the streaming window.

request.description: The tiny request the app times for ping and jitter. The app sends one unmeasured warm-up first and then six timed samples; this sends one.

exec: pm.test('serves raw bytes, not a document', () => {
// Cloudflare reports its own view of the TCP connection in Server-Timing.
// rtt there is in microseconds; it excludes the HTTP and TLS overhead that
// the app's ping (and Postman's response time) include.
pm.test('reports connection timing in Server-Timing', () => pm.expect(rtt, 'rtt in Server-Timing').to.not.equal(null));

request.description: One download chunk. Change `chunkBytes` to try other sizes; above about 10 MB, repeated runs start getting 429 (see request 4).

exec: pm.test('responds 200 (429 means rate-limited; see request 4)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
// Rough single-stream figure: responseTime includes setup and TTFB.
console.log(`Download: ${(requested / 1e6).toFixed(1)} MB in ${pm.response.responseTime} ms, ~${mbps.toFixed(0)} Mbps single-stream`);

request.description: One upload chunk. The pre-request script builds a payload of `uploadBytes` bytes, like the app's repeating-pattern blob.

exec: // Build the payload at run time rather than storing 1 MB in the collection.
console.log(`Upload: ${(sent / 1e6).toFixed(1)} MB in ${pm.response.responseTime} ms, ~${mbps.toFixed(0)} Mbps single-stream`);

request.description:
Steps through the app's download sizes (CHUNK_LADDER in speedtest.js). Cloudflare rate-limits by bytes requested, so a 25 MB request is refused with 429 once a client has pulled a lot recently. On a 429 this request steps down to the next size and runs itself again — 25 MB, 10 MB, 5 MB, 1 MB — until Cloudflare accepts. Unlike the app, which shares one size across four streams and keeps retrying at 1 MB until its window closes, this stops and fails if 1 MB is refused too.

The retry uses setNextRequest, which only works in the Collection Runner or Newman. Sent on its own from the request tab it makes a single attempt.

If the first attempt succeeds, you have not been rate-limited; run the collection a few times in a row to see the 429 path.

exec: // Newer runners expose pm.execution.setNextRequest; older ones only postman.*.
pm.test(`${size / 1e6} MB throttled (429): stepping down`, () => pm.response.to.have.status(429));
// Reset for the next run whatever happened, so a failure here cannot
// leave the collection stuck at a small size.
pm.test(`settles on a size Cloudflare accepts (${size / 1e6} MB)`, () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
console.log(`Accepted at ${size / 1e6} MB after ${rung} step(s) down, ~${mbps.toFixed(0)} Mbps single-stream`);
